title: Remember, not everyone is your player
author: igcorrec
selftext:
Hey all, i've been working on a small browser game called [SnapFC.com](http://SnapFC.com) for the past month or so, and one thing I've learned is that finding the right audience is almost as important as building the game itself.

Early on, I thought soccer fans, mobile, and casual players to all react the same way... they didn't.

People bounced immediately. Some loved it. Some gave feedback that completely changed how I thought about the game.

The biggest lesson for me, not everyone is your player and that's okay.

It's easy to get discouraged when people don't "get it" but sometimes you're simply showing the game to the wrong audience. At the same time, the right audience will often tell you exactly how to make it better if you're willing to listen.

I'm still learning, still iterating and still making mistakes but that's been one of the most valuable lessons so far.

For anyone building a game... keep shipping, keep listening and don't let a few negative reactions convince you to quit!!
